stem.en: Kabir says: "If the host evolves a lock the parasite can never open, the race ends." Why does that not happen?

text.en: Every lock is a protein, and the parasite's key is a protein, and proteins change by mutation on both sides. No lock is unopenable, only unopened so far. And a lock that also stops the host's own molecules from fitting costs the host.
It does happen; that is how immunity works.

feedback.en: Immunity to one strain lasts until the strain changes. Flu shots change every year for this reason.

text.en: The parasite would just eat something else.

feedback.en: Some do. Most are shaped for one host, and a switch is itself an arms race with the new host.
Locks are proteins, from IV.5, and a one-letter change reshapes them. The sickle lock is exactly that.

explanation.en: Both sides are made of the same changeable stuff. Any move can be answered. The race has no end because neither side can stop mutating.
